title: Tangzhong Pull-Apart Loaf
description: A soft, airy loaf with a tender crumb, made using tangzhong and hand-rolled sections for perfect pull-apart perfection.

method.instruction: Make the tangzhong by cooking 30 g flour with 190 ml water until thickened. Let cool.
Mix all dry ingredients (flour, salt, bread improver, yeast) in a large bowl.
Add tangzhong, water, and oil to the dry mix. Knead by hand until smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise for the first proof until doubled in size.
Perform a gentle second knead after the first rise to redistribute air and improve crumb.
Divide the dough into three equal portions.
Roll each portion into a loose ball, then use the “tiny tension trick”: cup it in one hand and tuck edges underneath while rotating gently, creating a smooth, taut dome.
Place the balls snugly into a greased loaf pan (approx. 8 × 18 cm), edges touching lightly.
Cover loosely and let the dough rise until puffed and slightly jiggly, testing with a gentle poke.
Lightly brush the top of the dough with milk before baking.
Preheat oven to 180–185°C and bake for 25–30 minutes. If browning is slow, increase to 190°C for the last few minutes.
Remove from oven and immediately brush the warm loaf with melted butter.
Let the loaf rest 5–10 minutes in the pan, then gently lift out and cool slightly before slicing.

notes.title: Notes & Tips
notes.content: - Small balls in the pan support each other and prevent sagging sides.

notes.title: Notes & Tips
notes.content: - Keep the surface of each ball taut to hold the shape during baking.

notes.title: Notes & Tips
notes.content: - Wallaby’s bakers flour gives a softer, smoother dough and a better rise compared to plain flour.

notes.title: Notes & Tips
notes.content: - Dust hands lightly when kneading if the dough is sticky, but avoid drying it out.

notes.title: Notes & Tips
notes.content: - Brushing milk before baking gives a soft, golden crust; brushing melted butter after baking adds flavor and a glossy finish.
